topic.title: Running an Incremental Translation
topic.shortdesc: Explains what happens when you run the translation agent on a project.

body.p: When you start a translation job, the agent first determines the translation status of each source file included in your selection. It then translates only the files that require translation. You can monitor and manage the job from its card, just as you would for any other translation job; see Following and Managing a Translation Job.

section.title: Translation Status
section.p: Each source file has one of three statuses for a given target language:

ul.li: Missing - The file has never been translated into this language.
Stale - The file was translated previously, but its English source has changed since the last recorded translation.
Current - The recorded translation already matches the current English source.

section.p: The agent determines whether a file is stale by comparing the current version of the English file with the source version recorded the last time its translation was updated, using the translation index. Files marked as current are skipped entirely, which is what makes the translation incremental.

section.title: How Files Are Processed
section.p: For a stale file, the agent uses the existing translated file as context when generating the updated translation. This helps preserve previous phrasing and terminology instead of translating the file from scratch. A file is marked as current only after its translated version passes validation.

section.title: Manual Edits Are Preserved as Context
section.p: Editing a translated file manually does not, by itself, make it stale. Staleness depends only on whether the English source has changed. As a result, a translated file that you corrected manually remains current until its English source changes again. When that happens and the file becomes stale, the agent reuses your manual corrections as context for the next translation, so your wording is preserved instead of being translated again.
